claim: The demo command restores three shipped rows on Postgres in an internal Docker network, signs the result, reports a corrupt backup, and removes its resources.
sandbox: clean GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner with a real Docker daemon; healthy and corrupt shipped SQL; verify both signatures and zero managed resources

claim: The one-click web walkthrough uses only sample state in the demo namespace, and Reset clears and restarts it.
where: landing action, demo banner, demo documentation
sandbox: fresh browser context at /demo/?demo=1; inspect storage namespaces, playback state, reset, and exit destination

claim: Restore Drill rejects public, loopback, HTTPS, and undeclared HTTP targets before Docker runs.
sandbox: fresh configurations covering public HTTP, loopback, HTTPS, undeclared internal, and one declared internal host

claim: With --json, stdout contains one report object; success exits 0, a failed drill exits 1, and invalid input exits 2.
sandbox: fresh demo directories with successful, assertion-failure, and missing-config runs

claim: A drill leaves its backup unchanged and writes reports and signing keys only to configured output paths.
sandbox: fresh directory with sentinel input and unrelated canary; compare source bytes and enumerate configured outputs

claim: The demo pulls its Postgres image when missing before it creates Docker resources.
sandbox: fresh Docker-compatible process harness; fail first image inspection and assert pull precedes network creation

claim: npm run build writes an executable Linux CLI and the complete static site under dist.
test: npm run build && node --test --test-name-pattern='distribution build' tests/claims.test.mjs
sandbox: clean clone; assert executable bit and home, demo, privacy, terms, and 404 documents

claim: The shipped cron and GitHub Actions examples run weekly, preserve reports, propagate failure, and keep credentials out of source.
sandbox: repository examples; assert weekly triggers, strict shell exit, encrypted secret reference, and always-run report upload
repository distribution files; assert LICENSE text and crate metadata identify MIT

claim: The documentation site uses no analytics or tracking cookies; its first-party cache contains only public site files.
sandbox: production-equivalent build in a fresh browser; assert same-origin requests, no cookies/local/session/IndexedDB, one first-party service worker, and public-only Cache Storage

claim: A first-party service worker caches public site files for offline reading after the first visit.
sandbox: fresh browser context at /demo/?demo=1; wait for the first-party service worker, set the context offline, reload, and assert the walkthrough and signed report summary remain available
